meta.title: My Autumn Book — Set 2
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Vocabulary and word meanings in the context of 'My Autumn Book'.

questions.question: In the story, 'The air is crisp' means the weather is:
questions.explanation: Crisp air is cool and dry, which is how the air feels when autumn starts.

questions.question: To 'investigate' in the story means to run upstairs and hide in the bedroom.
questions.explanation: False. To 'investigate' means to go outside and search for signs of autumn.

questions.question: In the garden shed, what is the spider 'weaving'?
options: A silken thread to make a web
questions.explanation: The spider weaves (spins) a silken thread, which is how it builds a spider web.

questions.question: A 'chilly' wind is very hot and makes you want to go barefoot.
questions.explanation: False. A 'chilly' wind is cold, which is why the narrator zips up their jacket.

questions.question: The woodpecker agrees that summer is leaving with a 'rap-a-tap drumming.' What is drumming?
options: Tapping fast on a tree trunk with its beak
questions.explanation: A woodpecker drums by tapping its beak quickly on tree bark, making a sound like a drum.

questions.question: The squirrel digs a hole to bury its treasure. The 'treasure' refers to the squirrel's winter _______.
questions.hint: What squirrels eat to survive winter.
questions.explanation: The squirrel's treasure is the acorns and seeds it collects and hides to eat when it gets cold.

questions.question: The dogwood tree shows off a 'crimson gown.' A 'gown' is a word describing:
options: The roots of the tree under the ground
The beautiful red leaves covering the tree like a dress
The acorns falling onto the grass
The bird nest on the branches
questions.explanation: A 'gown' is a long dress. The author compares the crimson leaves covering the tree to a beautiful gown.

questions.question: Sort the colors of trees in the fall celebration based on their descriptions:
questions.explanation: Dogwood (crimson), oak (rust brown), and maple (red) are red/brown. Ash (yellow) and aspen (gold) are yellow/gold.

questions.question: In the phrase 'crickets chirruping in the clover,' 'chirruping' means the crickets are making high, short sounds.
questions.explanation: True. Chirruping is the sound crickets make, which is another word for chirping.

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe how the leaves move in the air:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'The leaves are spinning round.' This is a sign of autumn winds.

questions.question: When the author says there is 'no time to delay,' it means the narrator must:
options: Rush outside quickly before the season changes completely
Wait for the sun to rise
questions.explanation: No time to delay means to move quickly because changes are happening fast in nature.

questions.question: When trees sway in the breeze, they move gently from side to _______.
questions.explanation: To 'sway' means to move slowly and gently back and forth or side to side.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show what happens to acorns in the wind:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Acorns shake loose in the breeze.' Capitalize 'Acorns.'

questions.question: A 'whirlwind of color' means the leaves are falling in a straight, quiet line.
questions.explanation: False. A whirlwind is a spinning wind, so a whirlwind of color means leaves are spinning and dancing in circles.

questions.question: What does 'blankets the ground' mean in 'A whirlwind of color that blankets the ground'?
options: It covers the ground completely like a thick cover
It makes the ground very hot
It blows all the dirt away
questions.explanation: To 'blanket' means to cover a surface completely, just as fallen leaves cover the grass.
